verdict: No new medium or blocker. Three introduced low findings (R1 Identity empty Manage menu, R2 Pulse Backup facts layout, R3 Notes undisclosed .secondary restyle), three nits, and two pre-existing lows. The Identity, Recovery, DNS, Drive and Pulse focus items behave as claimed at runtime. Shared ky-ui bytes are unchanged.

findings.summary: Empty "Manage" disclosure for a delegated helpdesk viewer on Administrator rows
findings.trigger: Viewer access {admin:false, helpdesk:true} opens Users; a row with role admin renders <details>/<summary> while every action inside is gated by full or u.role !== "admin"
findings.impact: A focusable "Manage <user>" control opens a bordered empty 224x10 px box (measured). Before, the actions cell was empty. No action, handler or authorization exposure is added.
findings.fix: Render the <details> only when full || u.role !== "admin" (the union of the item guards); otherwise leave the cell empty or show a short "No actions" note.

findings.summary: table-roles.mjs uses Playwright getByRole/ariaSnapshot on synthetic markup. These compute roles from the DOM, not from the browser accessibility tree
findings.trigger: UI-VERIFICATION.md cites it as "Chromium keeps the table roles"
findings.impact: The claim is true, but the cited evidence is a proxy. Non-Chromium semantics remain unproven.
findings.fix: Use CDP Accessibility.getFullAXTree on the real page, or add explicit role=table/rowgroup/row/columnheader/cell so semantics do not depend on CSS display.

findings.verification_result: Claim CONFIRMED independently on the real app: CDP AX tree at 390 px has table 1, rowgroup 1, row 2, columnheader 6, cell 6, and no LayoutTable fallback. Firefox and WebKit are UNKNOWN.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus on a partly visible destination in the phone nav row does not scroll it into view
findings.trigger: 390 px, 16 shared workspaces (appended client-side), Tab along the row
findings.impact: Chromium 153 and Firefox 155 do not scroll partly visible focus targets, so odd-numbered long workspace names show about 60 px and "Recovery" 10 px when focused. The focused item is never entirely hidden, so it is not a 2.4.11 AA failure by the letter. The current destination after selection IS revealed (the new effect works), and the page is not scrolled.
findings.fix: Reveal on focusin using the same logic as the selection effect (and in other F6 overflow rows).
